slides.body: Lab 26.7. Add workflow 7, and after the run, open the run's summary page and find the artifact with its name, and the place where its digest is shown.
Five mistakes to watch for.

items: A job-level permissions block that names only the extra permission. Root cause: the job-level block replaces the workflow-level one, so every permission not named becomes none, including contents: read.
Writing @v10 for astral-sh/setup-uv. Root cause: that action has no floating major tag since version 8.
Deploying by the image tag main or latest. Root cause: both are names that move; they do not identify what was tested.
Deleting a Git tag to undo a release. Root cause: the tag push already started the workflows with a matching filter, and deleting the tag does not unpublish the image.
Leaving an old action major in place because the run is green. Root cause: an action that declares Node 20 is executed on Node 24, a configuration its authors did not test.

slides.body: Read the rest of section 20A.13 and sections 20A.14 to 20A.18 of Chapter 20A.
That one old line holds no surprise for you now: you can say what it names, what runs it, and how to pin it.

beats.text: Five mistakes to watch for.
beats.tele: Five mistakes to watch for.

beats.text: A job-level permissions block that names only the extra permission. Root cause: the job-level block replaces the workflow-level one, so every permission not named becomes none, including contents: read.
beats.tele: A job-level `permissions` block that names only the extra permission. Root cause: the job-level block replaces the workflow-level one, so every permission not named becomes none, including `contents: read`.

beats.text: Writing @v10 for astral-sh/setup-uv. Root cause: that action has no floating major tag since version 8.
beats.tele: Writing `@v10` for `astral-sh/setup-uv`. Root cause: that action has no floating major tag since version 8.

beats.text: Deploying by the image tag main or latest. Root cause: both are names that move; they do not identify what was tested.
beats.tele: Deploying by the image tag `main` or `latest`. Root cause: both are names that move; they do not identify what was tested.

beats.text: Deleting a Git tag to undo a release. Root cause: the tag push already started the workflows with a matching filter, and deleting the tag does not unpublish the image.
beats.tele: Deleting a Git tag to undo a release. Root cause: the tag push already started the workflows with a matching filter, and deleting the tag does not unpublish the image.

beats.text: Leaving an old action major in place because the run is green. Root cause: an action that declares Node 20 is executed on Node 24, a configuration its authors did not test.
beats.tele: Leaving an old action major in place because the run is green. Root cause: an action that declares Node 20 is executed on Node 24, a configuration its authors did not test.

beats.text: Now, out of the lab. A team that serves models has a release workflow written in 2024. It references actions by major tag and runs on ubuntu-latest. In the autumn of 2026 two things happen within weeks, and neither is a commit to the repository. On the twenty-third of September, Node 20 stops being available, and their older action majors are executed on Node 24. Between the nineteenth of October and the nineteenth of November, by the schedule GitHub announced, ubuntu-latest migrates to Ubuntu 26.04.
beats.tele: Now, out of the lab. A team that serves models has a release workflow written in 2024. It references actions by major tag and runs on `ubuntu-latest`. In the autumn of 2026 two things happen within weeks, and neither is a commit to the repository. On the twenty-third of September, Node 20 stops being available, and their older action majors are executed on Node 24. Between the nineteenth of October and the nineteenth of November, by the schedule GitHub announced, `ubuntu-latest` migrates to Ubuntu 26.04.

beats.text: If a release then fails, the team has nothing to bisect: the repository didn't change. That's the cost of floating references.
